approachQuestion.prompt: A timeline contains integer levels a[0..n-1]. Return the largest distance j-i over all i<j with a[i] ≤ a[j], or 0 if no such pair exists. Equal levels qualify. Example: [6, 0, 8, 2, 1, 5] returns 4, using positions 1 and 5. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Build a stack of indices of strictly decreasing prefix minima. Scan j from right to left; while the top index i satisfies a[i] ≤ a[j], update the answer with j-i if positive and pop i.
options.feedback: An earlier left endpoint with no larger value dominates a later one. The first feasible right endpoint encountered in reverse order is farthest for each stored left endpoint.

options.text: For each i find only its nearest later value at least a[i], and maximize those distances.
options.feedback: The farthest qualifying endpoint is needed. For [1, 2, 3], nearest distances are 1, while the answer is 2.

options.text: Find the earliest global minimum and return its distance to the last position.
options.feedback: A preceding position can give a wider feasible pair. For [1, 0, 2], the answer is 2 from positions 0 and 2, not 1.

options.text: Test a[i] ≤ a[j] for every i<j and keep the greatest distance.
options.feedback: This is correct but enumerates all endpoint pairs, creating quadratic work even when there is no feasible pair.

feedback.reason: Keep only undominated left endpoints, then settle their farthest feasible right endpoints in reverse order.
details: Store only each new strict prefix minimum. Visit right endpoints from the end backward. Pop every stored left endpoint whose value is no greater than the right value and update the maximum positive distance.

Only new strict prefix minima can improve a left endpoint: a later larger value is dominated by an earlier smaller one. Scan right endpoints backward so the first qualifying one gives each left candidate its largest distance.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For prefix-minima-reverse-sweep, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the timeline length. Keep one index stack and a scalar answer, without copying input.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build and consume each prefix-minimum candidate once.
details: Only new prefix minima enter the candidate stack; a candidate is removed permanently at its farthest qualifying right endpoint. Thus build, reverse scan, and all pops add to O(n). A strictly decreasing input stores n candidates, so the stack is O(n) auxiliary space. Scanning each right endpoint afresh for every left candidate is not this method.
